sections.content: Reported speech introduces another person's words through verbs such as decir, afirmar and declarar. At this level, focus on the basic structure: subject + reporting verb + que + reported statement. When the original statement is in the past, Spanish often moves the reported verb into an appropriate past form.

items.spanish: El periodista dijo que el objeto había aparecido sobre la ciudad.
items.english: The journalist said that the object had appeared over the city.

items.spanish: La testigo afirmó que había visto una luz desde su ventana.
items.english: The witness stated that she had seen a light from her window.

items.spanish: El alcalde declaró que no conocía todos los detalles.
items.english: The mayor stated that he did not know all the details.

items.spanish: Circulaba un rumor que decía que el fenómeno podía repetirse.
items.english: A rumour was circulating saying that the phenomenon could happen again.

sections.content: The basic reported-speech pattern is decir/afirmar/declarar + que + statement. Keep the reported statement grammatically consistent with its time reference.
